Create an edgeR object

Source: R/create_object.R
create_edger_obj.Rd

Converts a ScreenR object into an edgeR DGEList, for example to use the object with edgeR or limma functions directly. All the edgeR/limma based functions of ScreenR (find_camera_hit, find_roast_hit, compute_barcode_statistics, find_time_hit, filter_by_variance and plot_barcode_hit) use it, so they all model the counts with the same normalization.

Usage

create_edger_obj(screenR_Object)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object, normalized with normalize_data.

Value

A DGEList with the raw counts, the effective library sizes, the groups of the samples and the annotation of the barcodes (genes).

Details

The DGEList contains the raw counts, as required by the edgeR negative binomial model (never normalized counts), and the normalization of the object set by normalize_data: the library sizes (lib.size) are the effective library sizes of the samples and the normalization factors (norm.factors) are 1. The offsets of the models, log(lib.size * norm.factors), are therefore the logarithms of the effective library sizes, the same that give the normalized counts of the plots and of the data table (raw count / effective library size * 1e6). For the "tmm" method the effective library size already includes the TMM factor, so it is not applied a second time; do not call normLibSizes (or calcNormFactors) on the result, which would change the normalization.

The object must be normalized, and every barcode must be annotated with a gene. The genes table of the DGEList is the rowData of the object.

See also

normalize_data, create_design_matrix

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
dge <- create_edger_obj(object)
dge$samples
#>               group lib.size norm.factors
#> T1            T1/T2 10671757            1
#> T2            T1/T2  9799724            1
#> Time3_TRT_A Treated  6824877            1
#> Time3_TRT_B Treated  9107354            1
#> Time3_TRT_C Treated  9717868            1
#> Time3_A     Control  9485195            1
#> Time3_B     Control  9016812            1
#> Time3_C     Control  9568624            1
#> Time4_TRT_A Treated  8933915            1
#> Time4_TRT_B Treated  9883209            1
#> Time4_TRT_C Treated 12325124            1
#> Time4_A     Control 10351136            1
#> Time4_B     Control  9180192            1
#> Time4_c     Control  9315365            1
